about: Labelled transactions for scripts/probe/detector-pass.mjs. Positives are exploit, attack and drain transactions from cases/incidents (a drain the victim signed records sender_withheld, never the victim's address), split by incident: tuning for the incidents the rules were designed from or tuned with, and holdout for incidents added after the rules were written, which no rule's detector_origins lists. Negatives are ordinary mainnet transactions in two splits: tuning, the 113 rule authors looked at, and holdout, sampled at random on 2026-09-27 after the rules were written and never shown to their authors. A negative whose signer is a known victim records sender_withheld as well. Every entry is a past transaction, so its label, sender, time and calls cannot drift. detected_by lists the medium or high flags reviewed as pointing at the attack; accepted_fps lists the flags on tuning negatives accepted as known false positives. The holdout split has no per-entry list: holdout_ceilings records each kind's medium-or-high count there, and a change in any count fails the run. Format in cases/README.md.

caller-value-used.basis: de81f0a (2026-09-26) replaces oracle-set-then-used (79c7813, written against Typus; OverfitAudit A1): taint through pure-only calls, fixed_point64::create_from_raw_value and vector decoding was built because the old rule missed Nemo, and its tests use Typus and Nemo 19Zkat1x. Its high grade at a 100x span and the info grade for the Typus keeper were set so the keeper's two tuning negatives read info. Tuned with every positive in view: the rule changed after the labelled set existed (6fb7342, 2026-09-26), and each revision was run against all 16 positives and the 113 tuning negatives. Following objects through earlier results and the product branch (an event stating the caller value times another of its numbers over a power of ten) were written from the Aftermath Perpetuals exploit's negative integrator fee, which reaches shared state only as fee times notional.

shared-state-jump.basis: 5359dbf (2026-09-26), OverfitAudit priority 1, which named Typus, Nemo, Scallop and Cetus as the transactions it should fire on; the wrong-source branch states Scallop's missing assert_pool_id as data flow, and its tests are built from Scallop, Nemo and Typus data. Its exclusions (list slots, zero moves, values at 2^127 or above, per-holder netting, the no-payee and conversion info grades) were each added to clear tuning negatives. It reads Volo at medium from cur_epoch_loss, seen while tuning. Tuned with every positive in view: the rule changed after the labelled set existed (6fb7342, 2026-09-26), and each revision was run against all 16 positives and the 113 tuning negatives. The value-share branch (a holder losing half or more of its priced value while addresses gain at least half of it) was written from the Aftermath Perpetuals drains that fell 13.9x to 30x, under the factor; its threshold was set on the 113 tuning negatives, where the largest such share was 6.8%.

unreconciled-gain.basis: db914d6 (2026-09-26), OverfitAudit priority 2, specified to flag Scallop's $142.5K; counting dynamic-field holdings and mints took it from 10 to 3 tuning negatives, at info. Tuned with every positive in view: the rule changed after the labelled set existed (6fb7342, 2026-09-26), and each revision was run against all 16 positives and the 113 tuning negatives. Pool events keyed by side and direction (token_x_amount_in, amount_y_out) are decoded since the BlueMove drain, which changes what the events explain; run against both new incidents.

outsized-mint.basis: 79c7813 (2026-09-26): the CLMM branch written against Cetus (OverfitAudit A2), the PY-mint branch against Nemo (A3). 2f243a5 (2026-09-26) bounds liquidity by the event's own ticks and drops the Nemo branch. Tuned with every positive in view: the rule changed after the labelled set existed (6fb7342, 2026-09-26), and each revision was run against all 16 positives and the 113 tuning negatives. The share-mint branch (minted share of a Supply<T> against the deposit's share of the object's holdings) was written from the BlueMove drain's constant-product LP mint of 122,000 times supply, with no protocol or struct name.

signing-key-replaced.basis: DetectV123 (v123/detect, 2026-09-27), written from Full Sail's Switchboard key swap H6d13yy4, which replaced the live oracle's 64-byte secp256k1 key. 32-byte strings and decimal strings were dropped from the key lengths after they matched transaction digests Full Sail's port objects keep (last_deposit_tx and the like) and a Pyth Lazer tuning negative's writer_digest, and a stored number that parses as base64. Tuned with every positive in view: each revision was run against all 61 positives and the 113 tuning negatives, and the holdout positives (Haedal, Full Sail, AlphaLend and the two wallet drainers) moved to tuning in the same commit.

price-off-market.basis: DetectV123 (v123/detect, 2026-09-27), written from AlphaLend's ALPHA-to-AVAX slot (the LazerPriceUpdationEvent and the AlphaLend PriceInfo rows keyed by coin type) and Full Sail's UpdatePriceEvent set at 1/100 of market and restored. The 5% agreement and 5x off-market factors were set before any negative was scored; the DefiLlama confidence floor (0.95, its top tier) was raised from 0.9 to clear the Volo tuning negative 5Yp9U9YY, where DefiLlama priced YBTC at $10.6K with confidence 0.9. The AlphaLend refresh 2NKoEGWv is accepted: the slot it flags really read the AVAX feed that day. Tuned with every positive in view: each revision was run against all 61 positives and the 113 tuning negatives, and the holdout positives (Haedal, Full Sail, AlphaLend and the two wallet drainers) moved to tuning in the same commit.

share-round-trip.basis: DetectV123 (v123/detect, 2026-09-27), written from Haedal's v3 redeems of LP minted through v1 (up to 1,763x per share) and Full Sail's port withdrawals paired with deposits made at a price set 100x below market. The 1.1x factor sits under Full Sail's smallest withdrawal (1.155x); the one-day window, the $0.10 exit floor and the rule that a position is scored only when nothing changed it between its creation and the exit were set before any negative was scored, and no tuning negative flags. Tuned with every positive in view: each revision was run against all 61 positives and the 113 tuning negatives, and the holdout positives (Haedal, Full Sail, AlphaLend and the two wallet drainers) moved to tuning in the same commit.

switched-before-execution.basis: DetectV123 (v123/integ, 2026-09-27), written from HeldOutV123's detector gap D4 on the claim::swapS drainer, whose owner flipped ClaimParams.initialized about a second before each drain and set its amounts about 4.5 s before. The window (60 s), the high bound (10 s), the $1 moved-to-others floor and the three field kinds (a flipped boolean, an address that gains, a number equal to an amount moved) were set from that design before any negative was scored. On the 113 tuning negatives, 64 read a shared object another sender wrote within 60 s (55 within 10 s) and none of those writes changed a field of the three kinds. Run against every positive; the three drains are tuning positives because the rule was designed from them.
